events_chronological: A boy is born in the family mansion and carried up to a nursery draped in white gauze.
As an infant he crawls under the furniture and comes to know the house by its undersides and its smells.
He is dressed in his first stiff clothes and taught to sit through long formal dinners without moving.
Grown, he gambles, drinks and keeps company with singers in the capital.
His father dies and he comes into the title, the mansion and the debts at once.
He marries a young noblewoman in the cathedral.
His wife dies of a fever, and the house fills with candles, black cloth and murmuring relations.
He sells the furniture piece by piece while the creditors start appearing at the door.
Aged and alone, he dies in the bed he was born in as a priest gives him the last rites.
The mourners disperse and the shutters of the mansion are fastened.
Labourers take the mansion down course by course while an old man leaning on a stick watches from the gate.
Nothing remains on the site but bare earth, and the palms and the grass stand where the walls used to be.
nonlinear_category_reason: Scene order runs from the latest stretch to the earliest throughout, with no present-day level the telling returns to. An old man waves a stick over a house being demolished and the whole of a life then unwinds from the deathbed to the cradle.
syuzhet_notes: The telling opens on the demolition and then unwinds the whole life backwards - deathbed, mourning, ruin, marriage, inheritance, youth, childhood, birth - before the final told bullet returns to the empty site.
fabula_notes: The reversal is presented as literally happening rather than as a manner of narrating: candles grow taller and the dead sit up. The bullets record the events themselves, in the order a clock would put them.
